title: B2+ · L6 — Giving feedback (360)
description: Dar feedback constructivo en ingles usando SBI (Situation-Behaviour-Impact) y radical candor. Balancear honestidad y cuidado.

questions.prompt: Curso de management. La coach explica el marco SBI para dar feedback.
questions.question: What does SBI stand for in feedback?
questions.explanation: SBI = Situation (contexto especifico), Behaviour (accion observable, no interpretacion), Impact (consecuencia real). Modelo del Center for Creative Leadership adoptado mundialmente. La clave es la B: se centra en accion observable, no en juicios de personalidad ('you were unprofessional' es interpretacion, 'you cut Sarah off twice' es behaviour). Nota UK: 'behaviour' con 'u' (behavior en US). Error tipico: fusionar B con I ('you were rude, which was rude') — deben ser distintos niveles.
examples: In yesterday's meeting (S), you cut Sarah off twice (B), which made her stop contributing (I). → SBI textbook
During the demo (S), you skipped the Q&A (B), and clients felt unheard (I). → tres capas claras

questions.prompt: 1:1 con un reporte directo. Vas a plantearle una critica constructiva.
questions.question: Choose the strongest opening for constructive feedback:
options: Can I share some feedback that I hope will be useful?
questions.explanation: Pedir permiso ('Can I share...') baja defensas antes de que se activen — tecnica de neuroliderazgo probada. 'Useful' senala intencion positiva. 'Always' y 'never' invalidan cualquier mensaje: son cientificamente inexactos y activan modo defensa. Error hispano cultural: en algunas culturas la jerarquia permite feedback directo; en anglo, la etiqueta pide siempre esta apertura pese al rango. Registro alternativo mas casual: 'Mind if I share something?' o 'Got a sec for some feedback?'.
examples: Would you be open to some feedback on the presentation? → question form invita
Mind if I share a couple of observations from the demo? → 'a couple of' minimiza el peso

questions.statement: 'Radical candor' means being harsh without regard for the person's feelings.
questions.explanation: FALSO — es una de las mayores malinterpretaciones del framework de Kim Scott. 'Radical candor' = Care Personally + Challenge Directly (los DOS ejes juntos). Ser duro sin carino cae en 'obnoxious aggression' (agresion odiosa) — precisamente lo contrario. La matriz tiene 4 cuadrantes: radical candor, obnoxious aggression, manipulative insincerity, ruinous empathy. Solo el primero funciona. Registro clave: la palabra 'radical' aqui = 'de raiz/profundo', no 'extremo'. Confusion cultural comun.
examples: Radical candor: 'I care about your career, and I need to tell you the demo didn't land the way you thought.' → carino + honestidad
Obnoxious aggression: 'The demo was terrible. Fix it.' → honestidad sin carino = toxicidad

questions.prompt: Un miembro del equipo lleva llegando tarde varias veces. Necesitas plantearlo sin sonar acusatorio.
questions.question: Which is the most effective way to phrase feedback about lateness?
options: In the last three standups, you joined 10 minutes late — the team ended up repeating updates.
questions.explanation: SBI aplicado con precision: especifico ('last three standups' — dato verificable), observable ('joined 10 min late' — sin interpretacion), impacto concreto ('repeating updates' — consecuencia real). Sin juicio moral, solo hechos accionables. 'You're always late' es falso literalmente (nadie 'siempre' hace nada) y activa defensa instantanea. Error hispano: sermonear con abstracciones ('time is important') — no accionable. Colocacion nativa: 'end up + gerund' = terminar haciendo algo.
examples: In the last two 1:1s (S), you arrived 15 minutes in (B), so we couldn't cover half the agenda (I). → SBI textbook
This week (S), the report was submitted a day late (B), which delayed the leadership review (I). → factual, no drama

questions.text: I want to flag something that came up in the retro — I think it's worth a conversation.
questions.explanation: Frase-puente tipica para introducir feedback en agile teams. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'want to' se reduce a /wɒnə/ ('wanna') en hablado natural; 'came up' con catenacion /keɪmʌp/; 'worth a' se enlaza /wɜːðə/. Colocaciones nativas suaves: 'flag something' (senalar sin dramatizar), 'came up' (surgio — phrasal verb neutro), 'worth a conversation' (merece hablarlo — no 'we must discuss' que suena forzado). Registro perfecto para 1:1 post-retro.
examples: I wanted to flag something I noticed in the review meeting yesterday.
There's something on my mind — I think it's worth talking through when you have a moment.

questions.prompt: En vez de decirle a alguien lo que hizo mal, quieres pedirle un cambio a futuro.
questions.question: How do you positively frame a request for improvement?
options: Going forward, it would be really helpful if you could loop in design earlier in the process.
questions.explanation: 'Going forward' + 'would be really helpful if' + accion especifica = feedback forward-looking (mira al futuro, no litiga el pasado). Investigacion muestra que feedback future-oriented se acepta 3x mas que past-oriented. 'Loop in' es phrasal verb esencial en team culture (incluir a alguien en un proceso o comunicacion). Error hispano: 'you must' — imperativo suena a orden militar en anglo profesional. Registro: 'would be really helpful' es hedging obligatorio para peticiones hacia peers o superiores.
examples: Going forward, could you send the deck 24 hours before the meeting? → future-oriented + specific
It would really help if you flagged blockers earlier in the sprint, ideally before Wednesday. → hedge + concrete

questions.prompt: Empareja cada expresion de feedback corporativo con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Cinco expresiones esenciales del feedback culture en empresas anglosajonas. 'Kudos' (del griego, informal-positivo, muy usado en Slack). 'Room for growth' es el eufemismo corporativo estandar para debilidad (nunca decir 'weakness' en review). 'Blind spot' (punto ciego — metafora de conduccion, imposibilidad de ver algo sobre uno mismo). 'Actionable' vs 'vague' es la dicotomia central: si no es accionable, no es feedback util. 'Track record' cuantifica trayectoria.
examples: Kudos on landing the deal — that was masterful negotiation. → Slack/spoken elogio
Your presentation skills are a real strength; delegation is a growth area. → eufemismo corporativo

questions.target: I want to acknowledge how much you owned this project — and I've got one piece of feedback that I think could take you to the next level.
questions.explanation: Formula moderna que reemplaza al 'sh*t sandwich' obsoleto: reconocimiento genuino + una critica constructiva especifica (sin cerrar con falso elogio para 'ablandar'). 'Owned this' = te responsabilizaste del proyecto en su totalidad (colocacion potente). 'Take you to the next level' es promesa de crecimiento — enmarca la critica como inversion en su carrera. Ritmo natural: pausa energica tras 'project —', tono ascendente/entusiasta en 'next level'. Contracciones: 'I've' obligatoria.
examples: You crushed the launch — one bit of feedback that could sharpen the next round. → 'crushed' = destrozaste = lo bordaste
Kudos on the delivery; I've got one thought on how to level up further next quarter.

questions.prompt: Tienes que dar feedback dificil a un colega senior mas experimentado que tu.
questions.question: You need to give tough feedback to a senior colleague. Which is best?
options: This might be tough to hear, but I think it's important — do you have a moment?
questions.explanation: 'Tough to hear + important' prepara al receptor emocionalmente (priming positivo). Pedir moment respeta su tiempo y su rango. Formula clave para 'upward feedback' (feedback ascendente): reconoce la dificultad conversacional Y afirma que vale la pena. En anglo profesional el upward feedback se espera y se valora, pero SIEMPRE con este framing tentativo. Error hispano: dar feedback ascendente igual que descendente — culturalmente inaceptable en la mayoria de organizaciones anglo.
examples: This might be hard to hear, but I care too much about this team to stay quiet. → carino explicito
I've been thinking about this for a while — mind if I share something honest? → tiempo de reflexion legitima

questions.statement: Feedback should always end with a positive comment to soften the message.
questions.explanation: FALSO. El 'sh*t sandwich' (positivo-negativo-positivo) esta desacreditado por research reciente: dilata el mensaje critico, hace parecer falso al elogio, y crea patrones donde el receptor solo escucha las capas positivas. Alternativa moderna (Kim Scott, Julie Zhuo): ser directo con warmth genuina — reconoce carino/respeto AL INICIO, luego feedback claro, cierra con proximo paso o pregunta. Error hispano cultural: sobrestimar la necesidad de suavizar — en anglo profesional los adultos son considerados capaces de recibir critica clara.
examples: Weak: You're amazing! But this is bad. But you're amazing! → suena falso, se olvida la critica
Strong: Here's what I noticed; here's the impact; what can we do next? → estructura moderna limpia

questions.prompt: Diste feedback y la persona reacciono a la defensiva. Necesitas desescalar sin retirar el mensaje.
questions.question: The person becomes defensive. Which is the best response?
options: I hear you — help me understand your perspective on this.
questions.explanation: 'I hear you + help me understand' desescala convirtiendo el momento en curiosidad genuina (no debate ni defensa). Regla neurologica: cuando alguien esta en modo amenaza, argumentar sube la tension; preguntar la baja. 'Calm down' es LA frase que MAS escala una situacion (implica que la reaccion es desproporcionada). 'Stop being defensive' meta-etiqueta el comportamiento — nunca funciona. Error hispano: usar 'tranquilo' u 'no te enfades' — traducciones directas que empeoran la situacion.
examples: I can see this landed hard — help me see it from your side. → 'landed hard' es colocacion metaforica nativa
I hear you. What am I missing here? → invita perspectiva, no defiende posicion

questions.text: The impact was that the client felt unheard, and we lost the momentum we had built up over three months.
questions.explanation: Ejemplo textbook del 'I' en SBI: impacto concreto ('felt unheard'), consecuencia medible ('lost momentum'). Fenomeno de connected speech: 'built up' con catenacion /bɪltʌp/; 'over three months' con weak form /əvəθriːmʌnθs/. Colocaciones nativas fundamentales: 'felt unheard' (sentirse no escuchado — no 'felt not listened'), 'lose momentum' (perder impulso — metafora fisica anclada), 'build up over time' (acumular durante). No juicio moral, solo cadena factual causa-efecto.
examples: The impact was that engineering had to redo two weeks of work, pushing the release back by a sprint.
As a result, morale dropped noticeably and two people asked to switch teams the following month.

questions.prompt: Un colega maneja brillantemente una situacion con un cliente dificil. Quieres reconocerlo de forma memorable.
questions.question: Which is BEST for giving positive feedback (praise)?
options: The way you handled that escalation was masterful — you kept the client calm and unblocked us in one call.
questions.explanation: Elogio efectivo = SBI positivo. 'Good job' es vago, olvidable, y no refuerza comportamiento especifico — el receptor no sabe que replicar. Formato ganador: nombra la accion especifica ('the way you handled') + adjetivo potente ('masterful') + impacto medible ('kept client calm, unblocked us'). Nombrar behaviour concreto activa el neurologico de repeticion. Error hispano: elogios genericos por politeness. Colocacion nativa: 'handle an escalation' (gestionar una crisis con cliente/stakeholder — vocabulario B2B universal).
examples: Your framing in that meeting shifted the whole conversation — beautifully done. → especifico + adjetivo memorable
The prep you put into the deck showed. That's why the deal closed. → causa-efecto explicito

questions.statement: 'Ruinous empathy' means being so nice you never share hard truths.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Kim Scott define 'ruinous empathy' (empatia ruinosa) como el cuadrante donde te importa tanto la persona que NUNCA le dices lo importante — el resultado es damage a largo plazo (la persona se queda estancada, la empresa se queda con problema). Es el cuadrante mas comun en managers de cultura hispana (donde 'no herir' es valor primario). Antidoto: cuidar tanto de alguien que estas dispuesto a tener la conversacion incomoda temprano — antes de que sea despido o crisis.
examples: Ruinous empathy: never telling a struggling employee they're at risk of being let go. → dano por omision
Better: caring enough to have the hard conversation early, when there's still time to course-correct. → carino real

questions.target: Let's zoom out for a second. Here's what I'm seeing, and I'd love your take on it — where am I off?
questions.explanation: Cierre de feedback dialogico y humilde. 'Zoom out' = tomar perspectiva (metafora de camera muy usada en meetings post-COVID). 'I'd love your take' invita al dialogo (no monologo). 'Where am I off?' es la pregunta magistral — muestra humildad epistemica (podria estar equivocado) y convierte feedback en conversacion. Ritmo natural: pausa reflexiva en 'second.', tono calido en 'I'd love your take'. Contracciones: 'let's', 'I'd', 'I'm' — obligatorias para no sonar rigido.
examples: Let me zoom out — here's my perspective. What am I missing?
This is what I'm observing. How does it land with you? → 'land with you' = como te llega/impacta
